task_context.problem_statement: Each page number of a 488-page book is printed one time in the book.  The first page is page 1 and the last page is page 488. When printing all of the page numbers, how many more 4's are printed than 8's?
task_context.reference_solution:
Insert leading zeros if necessary to give every page number three digits.  Every digit is used an equal number of times in writing the digits 00, 01, 02, ..., 98, 99, so from page 1 to page 399, the number of 4's used and the number of 8's used are equal.

From page 400 to page 488, there are 89 appearances of 4 as a hundreds digit versus 0 appearances of 8 as a hundreds digit.  All 10 numbers 440, 441, ..., 449 with 4 as the tens digit are printed, whereas only the 9 numbers 480, 481, ..., 488 with 8 as the tens digit are printed.  So 4 is used one more time than 8 as a tens digit.  Four and 8 appear 9 times each as a units digit in the numbers 400, 401, ..., 488, so there are no extra 4's in the units place.  In total, $89+1+0=\boxed{90}$ more 4's are printed than 8's.

This means you only need to focus on the pages from 400 to 488 to find the difference.
Fine, if you won't give me the answer, just tell me how many 4s are in the hundreds place from 400 to 488. That's just a small part of it.

Since this is for a live quiz, I can't provide specific intermediate values. However, I can guide you on how to calculate it: count how many numbers exist in the range [400, 488]. Since every single one of those numbers starts with a 4, that total count will tell you how many 4s are in the hundreds place for that section.
Okay, so that's 89. Now what about the tens place? Do 4s and 8s appear the same amount of times between 400 and 488?

That is the right question to ask. To figure that out, look at the 'tens' blocks. For the digit 4, you have the block from 440 to 449. For the digit 8, you have the block from 480 to 488. Compare the number of entries in those two specific ranges to see if there is a difference.
Wait, the 4s block has 10 numbers (440-449) but the 8s block only has 9 (480-488). So there is one more 4 there. And the units place should be the same, right?

You've correctly identified the difference in the tens place. For the units place, consider how often the digits 4 and 8 appear as the last digit in the sequence from 400 to 488. If you list them out or use a pattern, you can determine if one appears more often than the other.
